chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from al-Hasan b. Musa from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:

Surely, Allah, blessed and exalted, disliked six characteristics for me, and I disliked them for the deputies from my descendants and their followers after me: trifling in prayer, lewd talk while fasting, bragging after giving charity, coming to the mosques in a state of major impurity (janaba), peering into the houses [of others without permission], and laughing among the graves.

key_terms.الأوصياء: The deputies or successors — referring to the Imams from the Prophet's descendants
key_terms.التطلع: Peering or looking into others' homes without their permission, violating their privacy
key_terms.الرفث: Lewd, obscene, or indecent speech and actions — particularly prohibited while fasting
key_terms.العبث: Trifling or playing — engaging in distracting, frivolous behavior that undermines the solemnity of prayer
key_terms.المن: Bragging about or reminding others of one's charity, which invalidates its spiritual reward
key_terms.جنبا: A state of major ritual impurity (janaba) requiring ghusl before entering a mosque

ai.seo_question: What are the six characteristics that Allah and the Prophet disliked according to Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition narrated through Imam al-Sadiq from the chain of Imams back to the Prophet Muhammad, six blameworthy behaviors are enumerated that God Himself dislikes. The Prophet extends this divine disapproval to his successors (the Imams) and their followers, establishing these as permanent prohibitions for the believing community. These six traits span worship (trifling in prayer, fasting with lewdness, entering mosques in impurity), social conduct (bragging after charity, peering into homes), and respect for the dead (laughing at gravesites).
